decisions.statement: Whose a transcript is, is the session that transcript states.
A transcript stating a session another seat is bound to is that seat's.
A seat naming another seat's transcript is put back on the seat's own.
The seat's own is the file beside it that the seat's own session names.
A seat is put back before any candidate beside the named file is weighed.
A transcript no other seat is bound to is the seat's own, however old.
A seat bound to no session has none put back, since there is nothing to put back to.
A seat naming no transcript has no transcript rotated.
A transcript the seat names that is not on the disk is not rotated.
A transcript written within the last minute is still live and is not rotated.
A candidate is a `.jsonl` file directly beside the transcript the seat names.
A file no newer than the transcript the seat names is no candidate.
A file any seat names is no candidate.
A file whose first record was written before the named file's last write is no candidate.
The answer comes only where exactly one candidate is left.
A record's timestamp is read off the record's top rather than out of anything nested in the record.
The opening records of a transcript have no timestamp.
How many opening records a transcript has differs by session.
A transcript is read for its opening bytes alone rather than whole.
The rule is decided from a reading of the disk rather than from the disk.
Nothing here writes.
No rotated session is kept.

definition: the transcript a seat should be read from where the one it names is another seat's or done
